text: Let us recap. Unpolarized light vibrates in every direction across the beam; plane polarized light in just one plane. It can be produced by reflection, refraction, absorption in a Polaroid, double refraction and scattering. Brewster's law says n equals tan theta p, where the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular. Malus's law says I equals I nought cos squared theta, after a first sheet that always halves unpolarized light. And because light can be polarized, it must be a transverse wave.
